_scenario: One "3d" PhysicsWorld on Rapier3dAdapter with Appendix A gravity, holding four static boxes — a 60 × 1 × 60 floor whose top is y = 0, a wall at z = -4 spanning x ∈ [-6, 6], a 0.25 m riser at x ∈ [7, 13] spanning z ∈ [-18, -2], and a box rotated 60° about +X at (20, 1, -5) — and five capsule characters (radius 0.3, halfHeight 0.5) registered as "kinematic-position" bodies under §42's "kinematic" authority: walker (moveSpeed 3, intent (1, 0.6), into the wall), stepper (moveSpeed 3, over the riser), climber (moveSpeed 3, into the 60° ramp with slopeLimit π/4), jumper (moveSpeed 1, jump() asked on every step) and faller (dropped from y = 20 with maxFallSpeed 6). A SweptCharacterSystem at PRIORITY_KINEMATICS (400) and a PhysicsSystem at PRIORITY_PHYSICS_SOLVE (600) share one SystemRegistry, driven 300 clean fixed steps of 1/60 s with an injected TimeState whose simulationTime is exactly step / 60. The per-step value is the D6 FNV-1a hasher over world.checksum() followed by every character's position, vertical velocity and grounded flag in registration order; summaryDigest is the same hasher over all 300 of them in step order.
_tier: same-runtime (§33), the same tier as golden/phase5.json and golden/force-fields.json, with one reason specific to this packet: a controller that consumes solver queries inherits the solver's tier. Rapier is compiled WebAssembly, state crosses the JS/wasm boundary as f64 → f32, and the wasm image is pinned per platform by the package manager — so every shape-cast distance and normal this controller resolves against is runtime-bound before its own Math.sin/Math.cos/Math.sqrt touch it. Cross-platform determinism is NOT claimed. The checksum algorithm itself is exact and cross-platform; only its inputs are runtime-bound.
